meta.notes: Route and delivery. No rate for thoughts. Directional, impatient with preamble. Marks every held piece across the flap. Mae has never read a carrier's book. He does not know what he carried.

threads.topic: You took something to 6C that Friday.
threads.source: S08, B08. The first rescue lever is on the day itself.

threads.topic: Omar says he learned who owned the windmill.
threads.source: JF024-A01. Owner put it back. The bank wanted it only instead of JF001; here it answers that line in another scene, so the beat is not doubled.

threads.topic: What did you carry down from there?
threads.source: 4.5. A concrete question gets the book.

threads.topic: Can a sender take back a held piece?
threads.source: Suspect chain, Peter. Makes the route book look soft, then proves it.

threads.topic: What else went up to 6C that week?
threads.source: Kept from a cut chain. Blank discs on the eve of the cut.

threads.topic: You ride the Corona line a lot.

co_e1.line: Ten past six. Six C. In her hand.

co_e1s.line: I've got eleven more and the bridge is backing up. Walk with me or don't.

co_e2.line: I deliver envelopes. Nobody's offered a rate for thoughts.

co_e3.line: The lady across the road. Walked it over to me herself and paid for the stairs. Six flights, a nickel, she says to me it's a nickel because I'm charging for the view. She was funny. Is that it?

co_w1.line: If the windmill has enemies, I'd appreciate their addresses. I'm trying to be a supportive friend. I can have them there by four.

co_r1.line: Which time? It's a route. You want Friday, say Friday.

choices.label: Did she give you anything to hold?

co_r1s.line: You're doing the thing where you stand there. I've got that from a dog on Vernon Boulevard. It doesn't work on me either.

co_r2.line: Book says. "Fri. 19 Jul., 6.40 p.m., 6C to Mr. Ewald, hold, first run Sat." She gave it me at the door. I put it on the rack, pencil across the flap, C.O., six-forty, so nobody can say I opened it. She does it about once a month, it's an estate, they love a Saturday. First run, down the road, eight-fifty. Done.

co_r3.line: Everybody gives me stuff to hold. That's not a question, that's my life. Friday? Here. Six-forty, six C to Ewald, first run Saturday. Read it yourself, it's not a secret, it's just nobody ever reads it.

co_rc1.line: Sender can. Comes down, says give it here, I strike it and write the time. Same Friday, look. "4A to Miss Q., hold." Struck. "Recalled 5.55." Mr. Wren. Twenty-five minutes. Something about a comma.

choices.label: Is there a strike on six-forty?

co_rc1s.line: I don't charge for the book. I charge for standing here.

co_rc2.line: You've got the book. A strike's a strike. There isn't one. Nobody came down.

co_b1.line: "Thu. 11 Jul., Fass to 6C, one box blanks, forty cents." Flat box, no weight in it, up six flights, and she checks the seal like I'd been at it. Is that it?

co_st1.line: In the tunnel, under the river. Half a second, on the left. Green. I've got nothing for it. I carry to addresses, and that one hasn't got one.
